question: For a typical annular dermatophyte lesion, the centre of the ring is the most productive site for KOH scraping because fungal growth is most concentrated there.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. The centre of a ring-shaped dermatophyte lesion typically shows relative clearing, not active fungal growth. Viable dermatophytes are concentrated at the raised, advancing scaly margin. Scraping the centre is the single most common cause of false-negative KOH mounts in clinical practice.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is false. The centre of an annular lesion has often already cleared, with minimal viable fungus remaining. The active, advancing scaly margin is where the dermatophyte is concentrated and actively growing. Always scrape the margin, not the centre — sampling the centre is the single most common cause of false-negative KOH mounts.
